fn.1: Literally: [[t:0]]with the commencements of his thoughts and ideas[[t:1]], that is to say, according to what first presents itself to his mind.
fn.2: The distinction that the author establishes here between the things of the intellect and the things that are within the domain of probable opinions is borrowed from Aristotle ([[t:0]]Topiques[[t:1]], l. I, ch. 1). The Stagirite recognises four species of syllogisms, of which the first two are: [[t:2]]the demonstrative[[t:3]], which is based on principles of absolute truth and evident in themselves, being founded in the intellect, and [[t:4]]the dialectical[[t:5]], which proceeds from [[t:6]]probable opinions[[t:7]] ([[t:8]]ἐξ ἐνδόξων[[t:9]]), and which is based on the suffrages of the totality or plurality of men, or only those of the totality or plurality of the wise, or the most illustrious amongst them. Good and evil, virtues and vices are within the domain of [[t:10]]probable opinions[[t:11]], and have no relation to God nor to pure intellect (See [[t:12]]Morale à Nicemaque[[t:13]], l. VII, ch. 1). The Arabic word [[t:14]]אלמשהוראת[[t:15]], which signifies [[t:16]]things generally known[[t:17]] or [[t:18]]famous things[[t:19]], evidently designates here things admitted by opinion and corresponds to the Greek term [[t:20]]τὰ ἔνδοξα[[t:21]]; the Hebrew versions render this word by [[t:22]]המפורסמות[[t:23]]. The Greek word [[t:24]]ἔνδοξος[[t:25]] having both the significations that we have just indicated, the Arabs have rendered it by a word which signifies [[t:26]]generally known[[t:27]] or [[t:28]]famous[[t:29]], although this word does not exactly convey the idea of Aristotle. Thus, for example, these words: Δ[[t:30]]ιαλεϰτιϰὸς δέ συλλογισμὸς ὁ ἐξ ἐνδόξων συλλογιζόμενος[[t:31]] ([[t:32]]Top.[[t:33]], I, 1), '[Lat.: the dialectical syllogism is that which results] from probable opinions', have been thus rendered in the Arabic version: [[t:36]]والقياس الجدلى هو الذى ينتج من مقدمات ذائعة[[t:37]]. For the word [[t:38]]ذايعة[[t:39]], a marginal variant, in the ms. ar. n° 882 A, gives the synonym [[t:40]]مشهورة[[t:41]], which is the term generally employed by the Arab philosophers. Here is how Ibn-Roschd expresses himself, in his [[t:42]]Abrégé de l’Organon[[t:43]], at the beginning of the [[t:44]]كتاب الجدل[[t:45]] (book of dialectic), corresponding to Aristotle's [Lat.: Topica].
